title: JSON Tables
tagline: Turns JSON-shaped data into relational tables.
role: exapump loads CSV and Parquet; a JSON document is an arbitrarily nested tree, and this add-on shreds it into tables. exakit data-load installs it for you the moment you hand it a .json file - it asks nothing, and one document may legitimately produce several tables.
installed_by: Automatically by exakit data-load when you load a JSON file, or from exakit marketplace.
platforms: macOS (Apple silicon), Linux (including WSL) and Windows x86_64. Not available on Windows ARM64 or Intel Macs: no prebuilt ingest engine is published for them.

quickstart.note: Pick the file, give it SCHEMA.TABLE, and the engine is installed and run for you.
Space selects JSON Tables, Enter installs it.

notes: The ingest engine ships PREBUILT. Nobody needs Rust or cargo - never tell a user to install a toolchain.
Several tables from one document all land in the schema you named, sharing the table name you gave as their prefix.

Quoted names are not optional: the table and column names come from the JSON, so `"users[].addresses[]"` and `"_parent"` need double quotes in every statement. A view with uppercase aliases (see the write example) is the usual way to stop typing them.

`exakit data-load` runs the ingest half only. The JSON-friendly SQL surface - dotted paths, TO_JSON, array expansion - is an upstream capability you install yourself with `exasol-json-tables ingest-and-wrap`.

troubleshooting.symptom: exapump will not take my .json file
troubleshooting.remedy: That is expected - use exakit data-load, which routes JSON through this add-on.

troubleshooting.symptom: No tables came out of the document
troubleshooting.remedy: Check the file really is JSON or NDJSON, then retry exakit data-load.
No prebuilt engine is published for this platform (Windows ARM64, Intel Mac). Load the file from a supported machine; on Windows, WSL works.

troubleshooting.symptom: object <NAME> not found, on a table you can see in the list
troubleshooting.remedy: The name came from your JSON and is case-sensitive with brackets in it. Quote it exactly: SELECT * FROM STARTER_KIT."users[].addresses[]".

troubleshooting.symptom: A column called something|object or something|array holds no values
troubleshooting.remedy: It is a marker saying a child table of that name exists. Join that table instead - on _id for an object, on _parent for an array.

snippets.title: What you get: one table per nesting level, linked by id
snippets.code:
root                          _id, <scalars>, <name>|object, <name>|array
users[]                       _id, _parent, _pos, <scalars>
users[].identity.contact      _id, email, phone          (object: 1:1 with its parent)
users[].addresses[]           _id, _parent, _pos, city, country, line1, line2
users[].activity.tags[]       _parent, _pos, _value      (array of scalars)

A column named `payment|object` or `items|array` is a MARKER, not the data:
it says a child table of that name exists. The values live in that table.

snippets.title: Read: join a child back to its parent
snippets.code:
-- objects are 1:1, so they share the parent's _id
SELECT u."id", c."email"
FROM   STARTER_KIT."users[]" u
JOIN   STARTER_KIT."users[].identity.contact" c ON c."_id" = u."_id";

-- arrays are 1:many: the child's _parent points at the parent's _id,
-- and _pos preserves the order the elements had in the document
SELECT u."id", a."city", a."country"
FROM   STARTER_KIT."users[]" u
JOIN   STARTER_KIT."users[].addresses[]" a ON a."_parent" = u."_id"
ORDER  BY u."_id", a."_pos";

snippets.title: Aggregate across the nesting, like any other tables
snippets.code:
SELECT a."country", COUNT(DISTINCT u."_id") AS USERS
FROM   STARTER_KIT."users[]" u
JOIN   STARTER_KIT."users[].addresses[]" a ON a."_parent" = u."_id"
GROUP  BY a."country"
ORDER  BY USERS DESC
LIMIT  10;

snippets.title: Write: ordinary SQL - but mind which connection you are on
snippets.code:
-- These are plain Exasol tables, so CREATE / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE all
-- work. What decides whether they are ALLOWED is the user you connect as:
--
--   exakit sql '<statement>' --write     admin, not sandboxed
--   exapump sql -p starter-kit '...'     admin, not sandboxed
--   the MCP tools in your AI client      mcp_readonly - writes are rejected
--                                        by the database itself
--
-- A durable, SQL-friendly view over the awkward quoted names:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STARTER_KIT.USER_ADDRESSES AS
SELECT u."_id" AS USER_ID, u."id" AS USER_KEY,
       a."_pos" AS ADDRESS_POS, a."city" AS CITY, a."country" AS COUNTRY
FROM   STARTER_KIT."users[]" u
JOIN   STARTER_KIT."users[].addresses[]" a ON a."_parent" = u."_id";

snippets.title: Beyond the kit: query JSON syntax instead of joins (upstream feature)
snippets.code:
-- `exakit data-load` runs the INGEST half only, so you get the relational
-- tables above. The upstream tool can also install a JSON-friendly wrapper
-- surface over them - dotted paths, array expansion, TO_JSON - which the
-- kit does not set up for you:
--
--   exasol-json-tables ingest-and-wrap --input <file.json> ...
--
-- Then activate the preprocessor in the session that needs the syntax:
ALTER SESSION SET SQL_PREPROCESSOR_SCRIPT = JVS_WRAP_PP.JSON_WRAPPER_PREPROCESSOR;

SELECT "meta.info.note", "tags[LAST]", TO_JSON(*) AS DOC
FROM   JSON_VIEW.SAMPLE
ORDER  BY "_id";
